In Quzhou County, I would stick with the familiar wheat-maize rotation on the same land, because it matches the local weather, the soil, and the way I know how to farm. At my age, I would not chase risky crops that need more hand work, more market watching, or more complicated management. I would finish the winter wheat already in the field, then follow it with summer maize after harvest. I would use improved or hybrid seed where it clearly helps yield and stand strength, but I would manage the field in a plain, practical way: fertilizer in moderate amounts, a few irrigations at key stages, basic pest control when needed, and rotary tillage because it is easier and faster for me than deep ploughing. Since no land area was given, I am assuming I am managing 10 mu total, with wheat and maize grown in sequence on that same 10 mu.
